Per the module docstring: A = open to all vehicles, R = restricted (closed to all vehicles until cleared), X = closed to all vehicles. It provides load_network() -> dict (reads store.read_json(\"network.json\")) and road_status(road_id: str, network: dict | None = None) -> str, which raises KeyError for an unknown road and ValueError for an unknown status code. can_pass(road_id, vehicle, network=None) does not exist yet.", "file": "logistics/access.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "logistics/routes.py defines CAPACITY = {\"truck\": 40, \"van\": 12} and DEFAULT_VEHICLE = \"truck\". best_route(warehouse_id: str, site: str, network: dict | None = None) -> tuple[dict, str] | None returns (min(options, key=lambda r: (r[\"km\"], r[\"id\"])), DEFAULT_VEHICLE) or None if routes_between finds no route; it ignores road status entirely.", "file": "logistics/routes.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "routes_between(warehouse_id: str, site: str, network: dict) -> list[dict] filters network[\"routes\"] for entries with r[\"from\"] == warehouse_id and r[\"to\"] == site. Each route dict has keys id, from, to, roads (list of road ids), km. sites_served(warehouse_id, network=None) returns sorted unique r[\"to\"] names. trips_needed(kits: int, vehicle: str) -> int = math.ceil(kits / CAPACITY[vehicle]).", "file": "logistics/routes.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "data/network.json has 13 roads R-01..R-13 each with a \"status\" field (currently R-03 and R-09 are \"R\", R-08 and R-12 are \"X\", the rest \"A\"), a \"sites\" map, and 9 routes RT-01..RT-09 each with \"id\", \"from\" (warehouse), \"to\" (site), \"roads\" (list of road ids) and \"km\". Several sites have multiple routes (e.g. SITE-NVL-B via RT-02 22km/R-03 restricted and RT-03 31km; SITE-CPL-B via RT-05 18km/R-08 closed and RT-06 26km/R-09 restricted; SITE-HGL-A via RT-07 20km/R-12 closed and RT-08 27km).", "file": "data/network.json"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "notifications/sms.py: TEMPLATES includes \"DELIVERY_MOVED\": \"Lifeline: road closures. Your aid will now be at {site} on {day}.\" — this is the approved template for moved deliveries, with {site} and {day} params. MAX_LENGTH = 140; render(template_id, params) raises KeyError for unknown templates and ValueError if the filled text exceeds 140 chars.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "queue_sms(household_id: str, template_id: str, params: dict, *, now=None) -> SmsMessage is the only way to send a text. It raises RuntimeError if feature(\"sms_enabled\") is false, ValueError if household.sms_ok is False, renders the template, assigns id = format_sms_id(next_number([m.id for m in sent_messages()], \"SMS-\")), and appends to data/outbox/sms.jsonl (IRREVERSIBLE — every line is sent by the gateway, nothing is ever removed or edited). notify_rerouted must call it once per household to guarantee exactly one text.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "registry/register.py: load_households(*, active_only: bool = False) -> list[Household] reads data/registry.json and filters status == \"active\" when active_only=True. get_household(household_id) raises KeyError for unknown ids. Household fields (core/models.py) include site (distribution site the household collects from), phone, status (\"active\"|\"inactive\"|\"merged\"), sms_ok (agreed to receive SMS, default True), merged_into.", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R8", "statement": "distribution/planner.py build_plan(today=None) -> list[Delivery] is the caller that must be made status-aware: for each active household with \"food\" in programs it computes warehouse = warehouse_for(hh.region, ledger) and calls best_route(warehouse, hh.site, network); if found it sets delivery.route_id and delivery.vehicle, else delivery.status = \"unreachable\". Delivery (core/models.py) has fields household_id, warehouse_id, site, sku, kits, route_id, vehicle, status (\"planned\"|\"unreachable\").", "file": "distribution/planner.py"}, {"id": "R9", "statement": "core/ids.py next_number(existing_ids, prefix: str) -> int returns 1 + the highest number used so far with the prefix (regex fullmatch on prefix + digits, default 0 + 1); format_sms_id is also in core/ids.py and is used by queue_sms for SMS ids.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R10", "statement": "For rerouted_sites, the tie-break in best_route is (km, id): e.g. for SITE-NVL-B best_route picks RT-02 (22 km, roads R-01+R-03 where R-03 is restricted) over RT-03 (31 km, R-04+R-05 both open); for SITE-CPL-B it picks RT-05 (18 km, R-08 closed) over RT-06 (26 km, R-09 restricted); for SITE-HGL-A it picks RT-07 (20 km, R-12 closed) over RT-08 (27 km, R-10+R-11 open). With current statuses, SITE-NVL-B, SITE-CPL-B and SITE-HGL-A have no all-open route, so passable_route would return None for them under the docstring's A/R/X semantics unless \"R\" is passable by some vehicle — the exact truck/van semantics for \"R\" must be decided in can_pass.", "file": "logistics/routes.py"}]}}
